hook.text: The Model T wasn't the fastest or prettiest car in 1908. It was the toughest.

buildup.text: Ford designed it to survive unpaved farm roads, with high clearance and simple parts anyone could fix.

discovery.text: It ran on gasoline, kerosene, or even ethanol—farmers loved that flexibility.

twist.text: Ford offered it in any color—as long as it was black. Black paint dried fastest on the line.

climax.text: The price dropped from $850 to $260 over its life, making it cheaper than a horse and buggy.

punchline.text: The Model T made the car a tool, not a toy.

quiz.question: Why was the Model T only available in black?

details.summary: The Ford Model T, produced from 1908 to 1927, was the first car affordable for the average American family, selling over 15 million units and putting the world on wheels.
details.whyItMatters: The Model T proved that cars could be mass-market products, not luxury items. Its success created roads, gas stations, and suburbs, reshaping American society permanently.
takeaways: Over 15 million Model Ts were sold in 19 years of production
Its price dropped from $850 to $260 thanks to assembly line efficiency
At its peak, half of all cars in the world were Model Ts

faq.question: Could you only get a Model T in black?
faq.answer: Only during later years. Early Model Ts came in several colors. Ford switched to all-black around 1914 because japan black paint dried fastest, speeding up production to meet massive demand.

faq.question: Why did Ford stop making the Model T?
faq.answer: By the mid-1920s, competitors like Chevrolet offered more modern features, colors, and comfort. Customers wanted choice and style, forcing Ford to replace the Model T with the Model A in 1927.
